concepts.definition: A tiny computer that puts the processor, memory and input-output parts on one chip and is programmed for a single job.
concepts.example: The chip inside a washing machine knows from its program when to drain the water.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking it is a computer that can do any job; it is designed for single, simple jobs.

concepts.definition: The name for an Arduino program. It contains the setup() and loop() parts.
concepts.example: You can write a ten-line sketch that makes the built-in LED blink.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking a sketch is uploaded once and then disappears; it stays in the chip's flash memory even when the power is cut.

concepts.definition: setup() runs once when the board starts; loop() starts again the moment it finishes and repeats over and over.
concepts.example: You set the pin's direction once in setup(), and you switch the LED on and off in loop().
concepts.pitfall: Putting a command that must repeat inside setup(): it runs only once.

concepts.definition: The two states of a digital pin. HIGH means about 5 V, LOW means 0 V.
concepts.example: When D13 is HIGH, the connected LED lights up; when it is LOW, it goes out.
concepts.pitfall: Always thinking HIGH means "on"; when reading a button (INPUT_PULLUP), pressed means LOW.

concepts.definition: The board drives an output pin; the board listens to an input pin. You set the direction with pinMode.
concepts.example: For an LED you write pinMode(13, OUTPUT), for a button pinMode(2, INPUT_PULLUP).
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting to write pinMode: the pin does not become an output, and the LED glows very dimly or not at all.

concepts.definition: The 0 V reference point of the circuit (ground). It is the path the current returns along.
concepts.example: When the LED's cathode leg is connected to GND, the circuit is closed and current can flow.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting to connect GND: the circuit is not complete and the part does not work.

quiz.prompt: Which is the most important feature that sets a microcontroller apart from an ordinary computer?
options: It must have a screen and a keyboard
It puts the processor, memory and input-output on one chip and is usually programmed for a single job
It can only connect to the internet
quiz.explanation: A microcontroller fits the basic parts of a computer onto one chip and is usually programmed for a single job. It has no screen or keyboard; it has legs.

quiz.prompt: After the program is uploaded to the board, what happens if the power is cut and switched back on?
options: The program is erased and you have to upload it again
The program stays on the chip and starts running by itself when the board gets power
The board waits for a new program
quiz.explanation: The program is written into flash memory and is not erased when the power is cut. When the power comes back, the board runs the program from the start.

options: It stays on all the time
quiz.explanation: setup() runs once and makes D13 HIGH. Because loop() is empty, there is no other command that changes the pin; the pin stays HIGH and the LED stays on all the time.

quiz.prompt: Which of the following statements is true?
options: A0 and 0 are the same pin
A0 is an analogue input pin, while 0 is a digital pin
A0 is only for lighting LEDs
The Uno has no analogue pins
quiz.explanation: A0-A5 are analogue input pins. Pins numbered 0-13 are digital. Carrying the same number does not make them the same.

quiz.prompt: How many digital pins does the Arduino Uno have, from D0 to D13?
quiz.explanation: Counting from D0 to D13 gives 0, 1, 2 ... 13, which is 14 pins. Because counting starts from 0, the last number (13) and the number of pins (14) are different.
